title: Prime-field regular local closed-point Kummer purity
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], finite Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], and the canonical Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], with the bounded-below closed-support adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction].

Let $k_0$ be a prime field, namely $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian regular local $k_0$-algebra [def-weil-regular-scheme] with $\ell$ invertible. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field], $d=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then the canonical map
$$A_k\longrightarrow j^!A_R(d)[2d]$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(k_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. This includes $d=0$ and requires neither finite type over $k_0$ nor excellence of $R$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.5, printed p.245, specialized to the closed point of a regular local prime-field algebra. This obligation records the proposition, not its old excluded proof.

proof.text: For $d=0$, [def-weil-regular-scheme] gives $\mathfrak m=0$, hence $R=k$ and $j=1$. The codimension-zero clause of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] makes the required map $1$. Now let $d>0$. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-strict-completion-input] to $R$: it suffices to prove the closed-point map for $B=\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$, with the same dimension and invertible $\ell$. Its residue field $F=k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is separably closed. The composite $k_0\to R\to B$ is a unital map to a nonzero ring, so is injective; thus $B$ satisfies the equal-characteristic hypothesis of the next step.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5, printed pp.244--245; fresh agent reconstruction by strict completion, Cohen/Popescu smooth parameter models, finite-type Kummer purity and supported continuity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-prime-local-smooth-parameter-models] to $B$ and $\ell$. Set $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ and $Z_a=\operatorname{Spec}D_a$. These are regular affine Noetherian pairs with compatible regular equations of length $d$, smooth over the polynomial-coordinate base, and $\ell$ invertible. Their limiting pair is exactly $j_B:\operatorname{Spec}F\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $\ell$ is invertible in the nonzero $k_0$-algebra $R$, it is not the characteristic $p$ when $k_0=\mathbf F_p$, so $\ell$ is invertible in $k_0$, as that input requires. Apply [lem-per-prime-smooth-coordinate-kummer-purity] with $c=d$ at each stage. It gives the canonical derived supported Kummer isomorphism $\gamma_a:R\Gamma(Z_a,A)\to R\Gamma_{Z_a}(V_a,A(d))[2d]$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathbf F_\ell$ and its ordered class uses the same equations.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, Propositions 3.2.4--3.2.5, printed pp.244--245; fresh agent reconstruction by strict completion, Cohen/Popescu smooth parameter models, finite-type Kummer purity and supported continuity.

proof.text: The small directed indexing poset, affine regular Noetherian stages and limits, preserved length-$d$ regular equations and invertible $\ell$ satisfy [lem-per-trait-test-supported-kummer-continuity]. Its derived-arrow square identifies the limit with $\gamma_B:R\Gamma(F,A)\to R\Gamma_{\operatorname{Spec}F}(\operatorname{Spec}B,A(d))[2d]$ and proves it invertible. Under [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] and [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], this is derived sections of the canonical map $A_F\to j_B^!A_B(d)[2d]$. By [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point], the small etale topos of the separably closed field $F$ is sets; its module sections are an exact conservative equivalence. They detect cohomology isomorphisms, hence derived isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. Thus the canonical map for $B$ is invertible, and the descent implication of Step 1 proves the required map for $R$.
